_note: The reconciliation comparison contract, as data. This is the authority: `docs/reconcile-comparison-matrix-v0.md` explains it for humans but does not define it, and scripts/check-reconcile-matrix.mjs fails the build if the modules and this file disagree. Every reconciliation report embeds this file's sha256 as `matrix_hash`, so a verdict is always traceable to the exact rules that produced it — which only means something because the checker keeps those rules and the code in step.

verdicts.matched: Asserted, observed, equal under the row's normalization rule.
verdicts.changed: Asserted, observed, not equal. Carries both values and the field path.
verdicts.missing_live: Asserted, observable in principle, absent from the response.
verdicts.extra_live: Present live, referenced by no spec selection entry.
verdicts.unresolved_binding: A package reference did not resolve to a live entity, so no field comparison was attempted.
verdicts.unsupported: Not observable from this source, so it can never be compared here. Never missing_live.
verdicts.not_asserted: Reported as evidence, never judged. Either the spec cannot express it, or it is spec-side structure with no live counterpart.

outcomes.reconciled_with_differences: At least one changed, missing_live, or unresolved_binding row.
outcomes.inconclusive: Input was partial or truncated. Never reported as differences.

normalization.nfc_trim: Unicode NFC, trim outer whitespace. No case folding — campaign names are case-significant.
normalization.code_set: Take `code` from each item, drop the display key (`name` on the campaign resource, `label` on gateway groups), compare as an order-insensitive set.
normalization.money: Exact decimal string, normalized to two places. Never parsed as a float.
normalization.currency_map: Compare per currency code; a currency asserted but absent from prices[] is missing_live for that currency only.

settings_rows.note: Spec lists every currency including the default; the API splits the default into `currency` and reports only the rest here.
Three shapes in the wild: bare code array, {code,name} objects, comma-joined string. All collapse to a code set.
Observable but inexpressible in CampaignSpec. Expressing it is future spec work.

package_model.why: A page may reference one package at several quantities — a bundle picker (1x/2x/3x of one SKU, with campaign offers supplying the tier discounts). De-duplicating by ref_id drops every option but the first.

entry_rows.note: Selection quantity is spec-side: how many units a picker option adds. The live package resource has no per-selection quantity and is correct not to. This is NOT an API coverage gap.

package_rows.note: Absent in the spec asserts one-time.

never_compared.why: Populated even when is_recurring is false — every one-time package reports interval "month". Comparing it classifies all of them as monthly. Carried as evidence only.

Dropped at normalization, before any value reaches a differ or serializer. The observed value is a bare 40-character string with no `cmp_pk_` prefix, so a prefix-keyed filter silently fails to match — the boundary is structural, not a pattern check.

unsupported_resources.provenance: Admin API Offers endpoints are in development. Offers are readable today from the storefront Campaign Retrieve API — a different observation source than this reconciler consumes. `unsupported` here means 'not from this source yet', not 'unknowable'.
The shipping API is global and read-only, with no campaign association.

price_basis.why: Observed package prices are list prices; offers are applied downstream and are not carried by this source. Every price row is labelled so a `matched` verdict is not misread as what a customer is charged.

coverage_rules.why: unsupported and not_asserted rows are counted, not skipped, so a report can never present 'nothing to report' and 'nothing was checked' as the same result.

known_untested: Cursor pagination: every recorded response returned next: null, so multi-page behaviour is unobserved. The normalizer surfaces has_more and the report goes inconclusive rather than assuming one page.
Whether ?sku= is exact or substring: a one-SKU recording cannot distinguish, so a multi-result response is treated as unresolved_binding rather than guessed.
